# matra

> NLP library: UDPipe structured parse, base text metrics, summarization, keyphrase extraction. Rust core with Python bindings.

## Introduction

- [Home](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/home.html): matra parses English text into sections, paragraphs, sentences and words, and returns measures, summaries and keyphrases over them, from Rust, Python or the command line.

## Tutorials

- [Your first analysis](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/tutorials/first-analysis.html): You will run matra on two short paragraphs of meeting minutes, then find four things in what it returns: the document's structure, the grammar it read off each sentence, the measures of each paragraph, and the measures of the whole document.

## How-to guides

- [Install matra](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/tutorials/installation.html): Install matra as a Rust library, a command-line binary or a Python package, then check that it works.
- [How-to guides](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/examples/index.html): Each guide does one task on one real text.
- [Parse a sentence into its dependency tree](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/examples/parse-a-sentence.html): The first sentence of Pride and Prejudice, parsed: every word with its lemma, its part of speech, the word it depends on, and the relation between them.
- [Find negations and modals](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/examples/negations-and-modals.html): Which sentences of a legal text are negated, and which carry a modal verb, read off each sentence's dependency tree.
- [Compare readability across paragraphs](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/examples/readability-by-paragraph.html): The three paragraph measures of The Federalist No. 10, to see where the essay is harder going and where it eases.
- [Summarize a long document](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/examples/summarize.html): The three sentences TextRank ranks highest in the opening of Darwin's chapter on the struggle for existence, 2,214 words.
- [Extract a document's keyphrases](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/examples/keyphrases.html): The ten phrases RAKE ranks highest in the same Darwin text as the summary example.
- [Read a Markdown document's structure](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/examples/markdown-structure.html): A short Markdown document with two headings and a quote, read into sections and paragraphs.
- [Cluster sentences by meaning](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/guides/semantic-clusters.html): Group the sentences of a document that say the same thing in different words, for example to audit LLM output for restatement, which lexical overlap cannot see.
- [Hand matra to an agent](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/guides/agent.html): Give an agent matra's own instructions, printed by the version it will run, rather than pointing it at these pages.

## Explanation

- [Introduction](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/introduction.html): matra reports the structure of text and measurements over it.
- [Concepts](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/explanation/concepts.html): Analysis returns one nested value. Each level owns the level below it and carries its own data.
- [Situation model](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/explanation/situation-model.html): matra reports the structure of text and measurements over it.
- [Programming model](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/explanation/programming-model.html): `Ingest` is where documents come from. `Engine` is what happens to each one.
- [One core, three install routes](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/explanation/install-routes.html): matra is one Rust core published three ways: a library on crates.io, a command-line binary built from the same crate, and a Python package on PyPI. The routes differ in what they compile and what they print about themselves, and not in what an analysis returns.
- [What the clustering threshold does](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/explanation/semantic-clusters.html): matra can group the sentences of a document that say the same thing in different words.
- [Pragmatics](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/explanation/pragmatics.html): Which call to reach for, and how to read what it returns: the choices behind the summarizers, the keyphrase extractors, the document measures, the clustering threshold and the models, and why each answer is what it is.
- [How matra runs](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/architecture/design.html): `engine.analyze(Ingest::path("essay.md")?)` yields a `Document` or a `DocumentError`.

## Reference

- [What matra gives you](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/capabilities.html): Every value the pipeline returns, by tier.
- [Domain model](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/reference/domain-types.html): `matra::domain` holds every type the library hands back.
- [Platforms and models](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/reference/platforms.html): What each of matra's install routes needs and installs, and the models matra downloads.
- [Semantic clusters](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/reference/semantic-clusters.html): The value semantic clustering returns, the model it embeds with, and its bounds.
- [Rust](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/guides/rust.html): You already have `matra` in your `Cargo.toml`.
- [Python](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/guides/python.html): You installed matra with `uv add 'matra>=0.2'` or `pip install 'matra>=0.2'`.
- [CLI](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/guides/cli.html): `matra` reads a file (or stdin) and writes to stdout.
- [Methodology](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/reference/methodology.html): What each number matra reports is computed from, how to cite the work it comes from, and what it does not license you to conclude.
- [Errors](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/reference/errors.html): Every fallible function in matra returns `domain::Result<T>`, which is `std::result::Result<T, domain::Error>`.
- [Boundary rules](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/reference/boundary-rules.html): Eight rules hold matra's hexagonal architecture in place.

## What is planned

- [Roadmap](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/roadmap.html): What matra does not do yet, why, and the condition that would change that.

## Blueprints

- [Blueprints: the process and the index](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/index.html): matra's design record. Two kinds of document live here, and the process around them follows the Rust RFC process.
- [RFC-0001: Record architectural decisions](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0001-record-architectural-decisions.html): Status: superseded by RFC-0019. We use Option B (ADRs). They live under `docs/decisions/` in the repo, follow a simple template, and are linked from PRs that bind to them.
- [RFC-0002: Pipeline vocabulary: ingest / decompose / parse / measure (+ peer extract)](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0002-pipeline-vocabulary.html): Status: superseded by RFC-0007. We adopt Option C. Pipeline vocabulary: `ingest -> decompose -> parse -> measure` with `extract` as a peer.
- [RFC-0003: Cargo workspace with `matra-core` and `rumi-nlp`](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0003-workspace-with-rumi-nlp.html): Status: superseded by RFC-0004. matra becomes a Cargo workspace with two crates: `matra-core` (the substrate, today's `matra` crate) and `rumi-nlp` (the matcher bridge).
- [RFC-0004: Stay single-crate; supersede the workspace split proposal](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0004-stay-single-crate.html): Status: accepted. matra stays a single Cargo crate at `mox/packages/matra/`.
- [RFC-0005: Supply-chain hardening posture](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0005-supply-chain-hardening.html): Status: accepted. This ADR records matra's adoption of the gh-guard posture, the manual setup the maintainer performs on GitHub.com and crates.io, and the items deliberately deferred.
- [RFC-0006: Abstract-tier vocabulary lock](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0006-abstract-tier-vocabulary-lock.html): Status: accepted. Reserve abstract-tier vocabulary now, in this ADR, without committing to shape.
- [RFC-0007: One pipeline: ingest -> decompose -> compose, with abstract reserved](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0007-one-pipeline.html): Status: implemented. The surface is one pipeline. `Ingest` carries the source variation as data (a string is a stream of one, a file is a stream of one, a directory is a stream of many); the `Decomposers` table carries the format variation as data; `Engine` runs the chain.
- [RFC-0008: Structural primitives are fields](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0008-structural-primitives-are-fields.html): Status: implemented. We choose Option B. Derived structural facts cross FFI as serde-visible fields with a single Rust implementation.
- [RFC-0009: Feats lookup accessor, Rust-only](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0009-feats-lookup-accessor.html): Status: implemented. We choose Option C. The accessor is Rust-only by design because `feats` already crosses FFI as a string, so a lookup over it adds no information to the wire.
- [RFC-0010: Embeddings: a Tier-2 channel behind an Embedder port, static adapter first](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0010-embeddings-adapter.html): Status: implemented. Embeddings are model opinion, not verifiable structure, so the roadmap's scoping principle admits them only as a specialist adapter with the tier stated plainly.
- [RFC-0011: Out of the box: configuration, paths, and one CLI](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0011-out-of-the-box.html): Status: implemented. We choose Option B for configuration and collapse the CLIs to one implementation with two launchers.
- [RFC-0012: The agent surface: a skill the binary prints](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0012-agent-surface.html): Status: implemented. `matra --skill` prints a `SKILL.md` embedded in the binary with `include_str!`; `--skill -r` lists references and `--skill -r <name>` prints one.
- [RFC-0013: Attribution and Citation](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0013-attribution-and-citation.html): Status: implemented. We choose Option B. The canonical attribution is the organization `mox labs`, with `yza.v@moxlabs.org` as the contact address, and it is identical in every file that carries attribution.
- [RFC-0014: The Distribution Matrix](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0014-distribution-matrix.html): Status: implemented. We choose Option C. matra publishes exactly four wheels per release, all abi3. Building matra from source, by any route, requires a Rust toolchain at 1.85 or later and a C++ compiler, because UDPipe is C++.
- [RFC-0015: Provisioning is matra's own, and a failure to fetch is not an invalid model](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0015-provisioning-failures.html): Status: implemented. We choose Option B. The UDPipe fetch moves into `nlp/udpipe.rs`, and the classification becomes the one the embedding adapter already documents.
- [RFC-0019: The RFC and EP process](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0019-rfc-and-ep-process.html): Status: accepted. matra's design record moves to a new root folder, `blueprints/`, and takes the shape of the Rust RFC process.
- [RFC-0020: Deprecate the config keys nothing reads](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0020-deprecate-unread-config-keys.html): Status: accepted. `models.udpipe` and `semantic.threshold` stop shipping in `config/default.toml`, so `matra config init` no longer writes them and `matra config show` no longer lists them.
- [RFC-0000: the template](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/rfcs/0000-template.html): Status: template. One paragraph explaining the change.
- [EP-0007: Five structural primitives (formerly plan i7)](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/eps/0007-structural-primitives.html): Status: shipped in 0.1.0. Boundary: rule-substrate. Lands before any `src/rules/` design work.
- [EP-0008: One pipeline, not six entry points (formerly plan i8)](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/eps/0008-pipeline-surface.html): Status: shipped in 0.1.0. Boundary: pre-publish surface freeze. Must land before 0.1.0 or never.
- [EP-0009: Embeddings as a specialist adapter (formerly plan i9)](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/eps/0009-embeddings-adapter.html): Status: shipped in 0.2.0. Boundary: first post-publish capability.
- [EP-0010: Out of the box (formerly plan i10)](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/eps/0010-foundations.html): Status: shipped in 0.2.0. Boundary: post-publish, additive to the 0.1.0 surface.
- [EP-0011: The agent surface (formerly plan i11)](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/eps/0011-agent-surface.html): Status: shipped in 0.2.0. Boundary: additive to the 0.1.0 and I10 surfaces.
- [EP-0012: The docsite on SvelteKit, with figures and examples](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/eps/0012-docsite.html): Status: shipped. Move the docsite from mdBook to SvelteKit with every page, URL and gate intact, then add the figure pipeline, the figures, and an Examples section.
- [EP-0013: The docsite's identity, drawn from matra's own output](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/eps/0013-docsite-identity.html): Status: in progress. Give the docsite an identity that could not belong to any other project, because it is made of matra's own output: a mark that is matra's parse of a sentence, pages that measure their own paragraphs in the margin, and figures a reader can scrub and point into.
- [EP-0014: Architecture guardrails: the boundary rules as semgrep checks](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/eps/0014-architecture-guardrails.html): Status: shipped. Seven of the eight boundary rules in `site/content/reference/boundary-rules.md` become mechanical checks, written as semgrep rules in `.semgrep/`, each tested against a fixture of the forms it claims to catch, and run by `scripts/check-boundaries.sh` from `just check`, the pre-commit hook and the `Boundary check` CI job.
- [EP-0000: the template](https://mox-labs.github.io/matra/blueprints/eps/0000-template.html): Status: template. One paragraph: what this plan delivers. For an EP that implements an RFC, in terms of that RFC.
